office_does: A U.S. Representative writes and votes on federal legislation, controls federal spending through appropriations, oversees the executive branch, and provides constituent services for the district.
race_blurb: Incumbent Pramila Jayapal (D), in the House since 2017, faces Republican Nirav Sheth, a Marine veteran and former police officer making his second run for Congress. Jayapal took 84% of the primary vote to Sheth's 10%.

candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative since 2017 and former state senator; Chair Emerita of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and ranking member of the House Immigration Subcommittee.
highlights: Leads the Medicare for All Act and backs an ultra-millionaire wealth tax [S1]
Authored the Iran War Powers resolution that passed the House 214-208 in July 2026; voted against the FY2027 NDAA [S5][S6]
Released a National AI Charter Act framework in October 2026 requiring AI companies to hold a federal charter [S8]
Co-chairs the Trans Equality Task Force; endorsed by Planned Parenthood, the State Labor Council and Fuse Washington [S1][S11]
Raised about $2.5 million through the pre-primary report [S3]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet backs an ultra-millionaire wealth tax; sponsored the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act of 2026 (H.R. 8085).

spending.basis: Leads bills to expand federal programs: Medicare for All, tuition-free college, housing as a human right.

safety.basis: Sponsored the Housing not Handcuffs Act and a moratorium on government facial-recognition use, pointing toward non-enforcement responses.

climate.basis: Pamphlet says she works to fight climate change and is Sierra Club-endorsed; no specific 2026 climate bill recorded.

experience.basis: Ten years in the House with subcommittee ranking-member and caucus leadership roles.

reform.basis: Says she never takes corporate PAC money and leads a congressional stock-trading ban and Supreme Court reform; FEC shows $280,500 from other political committees, so not a full pole_b case.

immigration.basis: Campaigns against 'lawless ICE and CBP actions,' sponsored the ICE Out of Our Faces and Dignity for Detained Immigrants Acts, and opposes rescissions targeting immigration services.

healthcare.basis: Leads the Medicare for All Act, framing universal healthcare as a right.

social.basis: Co-chairs the Trans Equality Task Force, sponsored a Transgender Bill of Rights resolution, and campaigns on protecting abortion rights.

tech.basis: National AI Charter Act framework (federal charters, pre-release testing, kill switch, strict liability) and a biometric-surveillance moratorium.

defense.basis: Voted against the FY2027 NDAA, for the Massie amendment to cut Israel military aid, and authored the Iran War Powers resolution.

candidates.summary: Republican first-time officeholder candidate, Marine veteran and former Lakewood police officer who owns Meineke franchises and co-owned a Normandy Park restaurant.
highlights: Campaigns on 'bringing law & order back to Seattle,' police hiring and mandatory treatment for repeat drug offenders [S1][S4]
Opposes Washington's new income tax, the Climate Commitment Act and other state taxes [S6]
Supports the girls' sports initiative and a biological definition of sex under Title IX [S5]
Immigrant from India who backs border security alongside streamlined legal immigration [S7]
Raised about $11,800 through the pre-primary report [S8]

taxes.basis: Campaign site opposes the state income tax, the millionaires tax, the CCA, the services sales tax, the estate tax and lifting the property-tax cap.

spending.basis: Promises 'military-grade accountability' over tax dollars and an audit of the CCA, while also backing infrastructure and police funding.

safety.basis: Law-and-order platform: hire more police, mandatory treatment for repeat drug offenders, let cities refuse supportive housing linked to crime; the pamphlet also states a housing goal for homelessness.

climate.basis: Calls the Climate Commitment Act 'a hidden tax' raising fuel and utility costs and stresses energy independence; proposes auditing rather than repealing the CCA.

experience.basis: No elected office; Marine, police and small-business background.

immigration.basis: Pairs border security and cooperation on removing violent offenders with streamlining legal immigration.

social.basis: Supports the 'Protecting Fairness in Girls' Sports' initiative and a biological definition of sex under Title IX; no abortion position found.

tech.basis: Wants to 'restore a business environment that supports technology including AI innovation.'
